name: productboard
label: Productboard
description: Product management: read features, products and customer feedback, file and link feedback, update features.

list_entity_types.doc: which entity types (feature, product, component, release, …) and fields this workspace has; no params

list_entities.doc: find features, products, components, releases; params: type[] (e.g. ["feature"]), name (exact), status[name], parent[id], owner[email], archived, fields[] (["all"] or names), pageCursor (from links.next)

get_entity.doc: read one entity with all its fields; params: id

list_entity_relationships.doc: parent, children, release and linked notes of an entity; params: id, pageCursor

list_notes.doc: find customer feedback; params: processed, archived, type[] (textNote, conversationNote, opportunityNote, …), createdFrom, createdTo, updatedFrom, updatedTo (ISO-8601), owner[email], pageCursor

list_note_relationships.doc: the customer and the features a note is linked to; params: id

link_note.doc: link a note to the feature it asks for; params: id (the note), data={"type":"link","target":{"id":"<entity id>","type":"link"}}

update_entity.doc: change an entity; params: id, data={"fields":{"name":"…"}} to overwrite values, or data={"patch":[{"op":"addItems","path":"tags","value":[…]}]} for list fields (set, addItems, removeItems, clear) — never both

prompt_doc:
Productboard is where the product team keeps its features and the customer feedback behind them. The API key comes from the platform — you never see it.

Lists come in pages: when links.next is set, call the same action again with pageCursor taken from that URL. Filters are query parameters with Productboard's own names, brackets included (type[], status[name]). Field names differ per workspace — list_entity_types tells you which exist before you write one.

Request bodies are wrapped in a single "data" object; pass it as one parameter. Read a feature before you change it, and link feedback to an existing feature rather than describing it again.
